question: It evaluates a patient with pelvic pain in which the simple Rx shows osteolytic and osteosclerotic lesions in the iliac and femoral bones. Point out the INCORRECT response.

options.opa: I would request a bone map including skull and rib cage.
options.opb: I would request a determination of bone alkaline phosphatase.
options.opc: I would start estrogen hormone therapy.
options.opd: Endovenous bisphosphonates such as pamidronate and zoledronate are an effective option in this problem.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Pelvic pain -> imaging shows osteolytic and osteosclerotic lesions in iliac and femoral bones -> suggestive of bone pathology -> 90% CHAIN: Bone alkaline phosphatase determination -> assess bone turnover -> helpful in diagnosing bone disorders -> 95% CHAIN: Estrogen hormone therapy -> may worsen osteolytic lesions -> not recommended in this case -> 90% CHAIN: Endovenous bisphosphonates (pamidronate, zoledronate) -> inhibit bone resorption -> effective in treating osteolytic lesions -> 90%
enhanced_information: Estrogen hormone therapy should not be started in a patient with osteolytic and osteosclerotic lesions in the iliac and femoral bones as it may worsen the condition. Requesting a bone map including the skull and rib cage may provide a more comprehensive assessment. Determination of bone alkaline phosphatase can help assess bone turnover and diagnose bone disorders. Endovenous bisphosphonates such as pamidronate and zoledronate are effective options for treating osteolytic lesions.
analysis: In a patient with osteolytic and osteosclerotic lesions in the iliac and femoral bones, starting estrogen hormone therapy is contraindicated as it may worsen the condition due to its potential to stimulate bone resorption. Requesting a bone map including the skull and rib cage can provide a more comprehensive assessment of bone involvement. Determination of bone alkaline phosphatase can help in assessing bone turnover and diagnosing bone disorders. Endovenous bisphosphonates such as pamidronate and zoledronate are effective options for treating osteolytic lesions.
